title: Día de los Muertos, ofrenda, photos, food, marigolds, and continuing bonds without appropriation

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source tradition/cultural-language synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no restricted ritual content, no claim of community authority.
limitations: Public sources support vocabulary, scene context, and review gates only; they do not authorize ritual instruction or tradition representation.
The record must not replace family wishes, clergy, chaplains, imams, rabbis, priests, ministers, celebrants, elders, funeral directors, local law, hospital policy, or community-specific practice.

Living communities govern their own knowledge; restricted, ceremonial, Indigenous, initiatory, family-private, child, and trauma-linked material remains outside public surfaces unless explicitly authorized.

moment.plain_scene: Long after a death, a family or community may build an ofrenda with photos, food, marigolds, candles, or objects, speaking to the dead through memory, return, and celebration rather than treating mourning as finished.

content_layers.observation_text: Long after a death, a family or community may build an ofrenda with photos, food, marigolds, candles, or objects, speaking to the dead through memory, return, and celebration rather than treating mourning as finished.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Smithsonian material anchors Día de los Muertos as a Mexican and Central American-rooted celebration distinct from Halloween, with ofrendas, photos, food, marigolds, and calendar distinctions. This record is anti-appropriation and vocabulary-only.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record exists to keep cultural and tradition language visible without turning the archive into a ritual manual or a representative voice for living communities.

what_this_is_not: not a claim that all families in this tradition practice the same way
not a substitute for tradition holders, clergy, chaplains, elders, celebrants, funeral directors, hospital policy, or local law
not permission to publish restricted, sacred, private, or identifiable family material
uncertainties: Practice varies by denomination, lineage, region, family, diaspora setting, institutional setting, caste/community where relevant, conversion history, secularization, and local law.
Public sources often summarize complex living practices and may overrepresent institutionally visible or English-language communities.
Public release requires tradition-holder review and careful family-language testing.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface may help a reader recognize the words they are hearing and ask the right local person. It must not tell the reader how to perform, request, refuse, or judge a practice.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Practitioner surfaces should ask what matters to this person and family, document preferences, avoid assumptions, and route to appropriate tradition/community support early.
language_notes: Keep diacritics, transliterations, plain-language aliases, and community-specific terms together. Never normalize a sacred word into a generic wellness term.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the cultural/tradition axis. It requires relevant community, tradition-holder, cultural-safety, and local-law review before any public surface uses it.
